data.narrative:
Alpha School, a Series A AI & Software company founded by MacKenzie Price and Brian Holtz, is evaluated against a universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public (Palantir) and 8 private peers spanning the same sector and stage. The peer set includes Reflection AI ($25.0B), Together AI ($8.3B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), and Black Forest Labs ($3.2B), among others in frontier AI.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given available data. The median valuation across the 4 nearest-stage comparables in AI & Software is $7.0B, with a range spanning $3.2B to $25.0B. This range reflects material heterogeneity within Series A and Series B frontier-tech companies, where valuations reflect asymmetric expectations around model capability, go-to-market readiness, and defensibility.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.9B to $8.0B, centered on a $7.0B median. Key uncertainties include Alpha School's specific product traction, capital efficiency relative to peers, and the durability of frontier-AI valuations in a market characterized by rapid capability shifts and evolving investor risk appetite. Absent revenue data, balance-sheet metrics, or forward guidance, the median estimate carries limited precision and warrants discount for information asymmetry.
